tagline: Farm country a short way below the Pennsylvania line.
intro: North out of Westminster and then east, the byway keeps a short way south of the Pennsylvania line through Manchester, over Prettyboy Reservoir and by Deer Creek, crosses the Susquehanna on top of Conowingo Dam and finishes at Appleton on the Delaware border. It is farm country, with hayrides and corn mazes in season.

Mason and Dixon spent nearly four years surveying the line in the 1760s. For people enslaved in Maryland, a Union state that kept slavery, an escape across it into Pennsylvania brought the promise of freedom.

moments.title: Union Mills
moments.text: The brick grist mill and the Shriver homestead both date from 1797. On June 30, 1863, the family hosted J.E.B. Stuart's Confederates, and the next day other Shrivers welcomed a Union general.

moments.title: King and Queen's Seat
moments.text: A rock outcrop high above Deer Creek in Rocks State Park, its legend of Native ceremony owed to an 1880 book that admitted to mingling fact and fancy.

moments.title: Fair Hill
moments.text: Old du Pont land kept for horses, with a thoroughbred training center, turf racing on Memorial Day weekend and a covered bridge near the nature center.
